stem: A child has fever, headache, and painful swelling and tenderness of one parotid gland. Which infection should the nurse suspect?
rationale: Parotitis—painful swelling of one or both parotid salivary glands—is the most characteristic clinical feature of mumps and may occur with fever and other nonspecific symptoms.
educational_objective: Recognize parotitis as the characteristic presentation of mumps.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_locator: Clinical features—parotitis with tender, swollen parotid gland(s) and fever
source_claim_supported: Mumps commonly presents with painful unilateral or bilateral parotitis.
correction_summary: Condensed the item and removed the allergy comparison that cued the answer.
audit_findings: Correct diagnosis is directly supported by CDC clinical features.
